The Technology Task Force welcomes and encourages public participation at the Technology Task
Force meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to
comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes or as specified by the
Chairperson. Anyone wishing to address the Technology Task Force is requested to fill out a
speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits the City to
identify persons for purposes of Technology Task Force minutes preparation.

Effective July 1, 2017, the Technology Task Force is responsible for developing a recommendation
to the City Council for the scope of an Advisory Committee on technology services serving the
community to be presented at the November 14, 2017 City Council meeting.

The Technology Task Force, at the direction of the Chairperson with concurrence of the Task

 Outline for Technology Task Force Report

  The City Council has asked the technology task force to make a recommendation
regarding the establishment of a technology advisory committee to the city government. Our
finding is that there is a strong and timely need for an independent source of technology related
advice to enable the city government to deal with an extraordinary number of technology issues.
These issues are now, or will soon enough, be affecting the everyday lives of the citizens of
Palos Verdes Estates. This report will detail the major issues of concern and make a
recommendation as to the size, constitution and method of operation of such a committee. The
key area of concern addressed by this report are: 1) using technology to connect government to
residents, 2)using technology to provide increased government transparency, 3)dealing with
current technology issues facing the city, 4) planning for future technology deployments, 5)
providing a framework for vendors providing technology solutions to the city.

  Because of both the working nature of this committee and the large initial workload of
high priority, high urgency tasks, a relatively large committee would be recommended. Seven to
nine individuals with a strong background in technology, and a desire to engage with the
community would be ideal. Much of the heavy lifting of the committee, such as the creation of a
Wireless Master Plan, would most likely have to be subcontracted out to professionals, but the
supervision of those efforts would fall to the committee, thus the requirement for a technically-
oriented membership. Since all of the work of the committee will ultimately be pointed towards
creating the best possible technology environment for the residents of our city, a strong
orientation to community feedback and engagement would be an asset. Members of the
committee need not necessarily be residents of the city, but priority of equally qualified
applicants should go to residents. If a highly-qualified applicant may have conflict of interest
issues these could be dealt with by recusal rather than denying access to valuable advice.
Meeting frequency should be no less than monthly during the initial year, or until the initial
backlog of urgent projects is resolved.

  In conclusion, we feel that the timeliness of action on this item is crucial as
developments in wireless technology deployment are happening at this moment that may impact
the future of our community.
 PVE Technology Task Force Scope Recommendations
  Date: 10/10/17

The Tech Task Force was tasked with recommending:

    Whether a Technology Committee should be created
    How that Committee is constructed (i.e. 5-9 people), guidelines, etc.
    Scope of the Committee

The five members of the Task Force concluded that the Committee be created, provided some
guidelines and identified and reached a consensus on the scope to be executed by the Committee.

Below are the details assigned to Lisa and Desiree on three of the approved scope items. Ghazala, an
active resident attendee, also provided review and input.

  -------------------------------------------------

  1. Improve Resident Engagement with the City
  a. Communications with residents
  i. Conduct open discussion about resident concerns
  ii. Conduct surveys to find out resident positions
  b. City responsiveness to resident concerns
  c. Accountability for serving the residents

  2. Government Transparency
  a. Solution: Adhere to National Standards and best practices for cities.
  i. National Standards:
  https://www.nationaltransparencyassociation.com/transparency-awards/
  ii. Best practices:
  1. Post contracts and invoices on City websites (like RPV does)
  2. Use PDFs, not scanned docs: allowing search on words and phrases
  3. Use self-serve – post all this information on City website
  4. Require suppliers email documents, so they are already digitized
  5. Keep organized in an intuitive manner; facilitating ease of access
  6. Retain, minimally, the required duration by law – optimally longer
  b. Benefits:
  i. Builds Community trust.
  1. Community trust is challenged by the City, engaging in 7 years of deficit
  spending; leaving residents concerned about where all the money is
  going. To build trust, engage in activities that show the City has nothing
  to hide and is receptive of resident concerns.
  ii. Provides greater ease of use by Staff; facilitating efficiency
   iii. Reduces costs SIGNIFICANTLY:
  1. Reduce/eliminate record requests costs paid by residents
  2. Reduce/eliminate city cost of records request because most/all requests
  are then facilitated by self help rather than City Staff time
  3. Reduces/eliminates costs for copy machines, maintenance, paper, ink
  cartridges, shredding, filing cabinets, filling efforts, retrieval efforts,
  duplication, faxing, scanning, offsite storage and transportation, etc.
  4. Entire implementation of this solution is under $500 and PVE Resident is
  willing to assist the City for free
  iv. Reduces/eliminates fraud and the perception of wrong doing:
  1. Inherent in full transparency is the elimination of opportunity to commit
  fraud. This is why the state of California created the CPRA laws.
  v. Is a Green
  1. Reduces PVE’s carbon footprint; as recommended by the City Mgr in his
  recommendation and passage of PVE’s “Climate Agenda”. Eliminates
  most paper, transport to offsite storage, duplication and shredding.
  vi. Prepares for a disaster
  1. Allows City to create a copy of the master digital copy and store offsite
  and, in case a disaster, the City will be ready to start up anywhere. This
  can be fully automated.

3. Relationship with Suppliers:
  a. Protect Resident Privacy and Security.

  Develop and include standard contractual terms and conditions in all City contracts that
  protect security and privacy of residents’ homes and personal information.

  b. Implement Quality Accountability into Service Contracts.

  Develop and include quality requirements into service contracts. Implement procedures
  of validation by City Staff to review and approve quality metrics are met before invoices
  are paid.
 CURRENT TECHNOLOGY

The Palos Verdes Estates Planning Commission schedule had no wireless telecommunication facility
applications for review in 2013. I found two on the agenda for 2014. Then in 2015 the planning
commission saw a sharp rise in applications. SB-649 will most likely allow telecommunications
providers with unprecedented access to public right of way and City owned infrastructure.
Therefore, it is vitally important that we focus the upmost attention to the installations that will
occur, as the current proposed expansion is a significant increase in the number of wireless antennas
throughout the City and will be with us for a long time.

As the wireless infrastructure in Palos Verdes Estates is expanded, so to will the fiber optic
infrastructure that provides transport of the wireless traffic. Currently the City of Palos Verdes
Estates does not have a complete inventory of fiber optic and traditional telephone lines existing in
the City.

The South Bay Cities Council of Governments has been granted funds to move to Phase II of the
proposed Fiber-Optic Master Plan for the South Bay. This proposal seeks to interconnect the South
Bay cities with high capacity, high-speed Internet access. The Council envisions this network may be
expanded by individual cities in the future to support their economic growth.

All of these improvements to communications infrastructure and “modernizing” City Hall will
increase the need for strong cyber security practices. Additionally, education of the community
regarding cyber security practices, current online fraud, and other technology related issues will
become more important moving forward.

Recommendations

The City of Palos Verdes Estates should form a Technology Committee for a period of 2-3 years
with following responsibilities:

    Develop and maintain a comprehensive inventory of telecommunications infrastructure in
  Palos Verdes Estates.
    Ensure that wireless facilities are sited and designed in a manner that is compatible with
  surrounding properties.
    Streamline the approval process for appropriately designed Wireless Communication
  Facilities.
    Responsible for permitting of new wireless facilities to relieve workload of Planning
  Commission
    Facilitate and promote new and expanded communication networks Citywide.
    Align the City's Code with preemptive Federal and State laws.
    Inform and educate the community regarding 5G wireless.
    Ensure that proper cyber security practices are in place for the City.
    Provide appropriate resources to the community to ensure they are informed regarding
  cyber security and other technology related issues.
 4 Future Technology
The TTF believes that PVE can best prepare for the evolution of technology by tasking a
Technology Committee to monitor and advise on a broad range of topics. In addition to
telecommunications, the everyday lives of the residents will likely be influenced by
developments both anticipated and surprising. We expect that the committee will evaluate, for
example,

  ●  Roll out of 5G wireless networks, and making recommendations to preparing the way
  ●  Fiber optic and Gigabit home internet service providers
  ●  Communications--ways to enhance city to residents real-time communications and
  modernization of our emergency communications approaches
  ●  Some members of the TTF anticipate revolutionary changes in the way people move
  from place to place in the next 5-10 years. PVE is unusual in the uniform distribution of
  needs due to a lack of a central downtown/shopping area, and in the number of seniors
  who could most benefit from public door-to-door service. Transportation technology
  includes driverless ridesharing vehicles, self-driving vehicle infrastructure, and
  application of ridesharing software to optimizing the existing public transportation bus
  system
  ●  Near term availability of integrated solar roof tiles can be investigated, allowing the city
  to inform permit seekers to consider more aesthetically desired choices

6 Technology Committee Concept of Operations
We believe that a Technology Committee should be established consisting of 5 or 7 residents.
The TC will monitor and evaluate evolving technologies and studies ways in which those
changes will impact the city. The committee will evaluate evolving technologies and
recommend action in order to optimally prepare for and leverage based on at least the following
criteria::

  ●  Anticipation of new technologies in a way to maximize and accelerate the benefits to the
  residents
  ●  Reduce the impact of the city operations on the environment
  ●  Enhance city operations transparency and enable the residents to have greater visibility
  to the operation of the city (is this really a technology issue?)
  ●  Improve city efficiency or enable the city to meet goals with lower costs
  ●  Optimize adoption of technologies in a way that maintains the city aesthetics

Because the members of the TC will need to see beyond just the technology, we expect that the
TC will consist of a broad range of expertise, and envision the establishment of sub-committees
made up of additional volunteers with more specific technical backgrounds tailored to the
specific tasking. We propose that the members serve 2 year staggered terms.
 The TC shall guide their activities according to the following principles:

  ●  The TC exists to serve the residents of PVE and further their interests
  ●  The activities of the TC shall be reported in a way that allows resident awareness and
  seek to enhance resident inputs

We recommend that the TC meet initially once a month to formulate a business rhythm and to
formalize the committee charter. Later, the committee will meet to form recommendations on
tasking. The TC will receive tasking from the City Manager or his designated proxy based on
recommendations received from the TC and/or City Council. The TC will have the option to
form sub-committees at any time to include members of the TC as well as other residents.

We expect that support to the TC through subcontracts is unlikely to be needed, but if needed,
would be coordinated through the City Manager/proxy. We expect that some assistance from
city staff may be required and shall be coordinated and approved by the City Manager or his
designated proxy.

A normal business rhythm would feature monthly public meetings to discuss tasking and receive
inputs from sub-committees. Each meeting shall be publicized to encourage resident
participation. Each meeting shall include a quorum of the TC plus at least one representative of
the city staff. Recommendations for TC tasking shall be made by the TC itself, based on
committee recommendations and resident inputs, as well as inputs from the city council as
provided by the city staff representative.
